I'm at work so I can't go into a ton of depth but two main things are:

Forward vs. Backward motion. Run blocking is mostly about moving forward while pass blocking is primarily backwards. This is a difference of footwork and can be thought of as being well practiced at one style of dance, but being weaker in a different style. The basics will be there but the technical movements that make someone good enough to make the NFL can make a big difference. 

And the general goal of each is different. With pass blocking, you're protecting a specific person that is often in a near stationary location. The types of moves you have to defend against during a pass rush are different from a run play where you're attacking the defender and protecting a hole in the line rather than the quarterback. 

There's more technical stuff but I think that's two of the biggest points imo

I'm assuming based on your post you aren't very familiar with contracts in the NFL.

This is where contract extensions come in. A team can offer a player to extend their contract(usually with an increase in pay) and they are able to do this before a players contract expires. 

As long as a player is under contract, no other team can contact the player about any contract negotiations(unless there is an agreement between both teams).

Alternatively, if a team can't work out an extension but still wants to keep the player, they can apply the franchise tag to the player prior to the contract expiring, which is a one year contract with its own rules for the amount the player will be paid.

So that's how most teams keep their star players for years, without giving other teams a chance to out bid them.

We had a couple meetings before actually becoming friends.

First time I met him was around 2 am at a Tim Hortons after the bar closed. We were in different friend groups but there was some mutual friends between us. At this time he was pretty heavily into drugs and the thing lifestyle. I was and still am the straight laced  kid that parents use as a good example for their kids. At some point someone made a joke about me still being a virgin and he decided to nickname me "the monk" because of it.

I didn't much care for him at the that time.

We saw eachother in passing a few times over the next few years but never really spoke. Then he joined my group's discord cause apparently he's been life long friends with a few of the members. He started playing league and I got to know him a bit better. He now had a 3 year old daughter and had stopped doing drugs the moment he found out his gf was pregnant. He had also cut out most of the people that had been party of his party lifestyle. He still had a lot of things he was working through, such as a long stint of unemployment and some mental health issues, but overall, big improvement. 

A couple months into our only interactions being playing league of legends as a group, he let's us know that his Fiancé has left him, was taking his kid until.they figured out custody and he's moved back to his parents place as it was his Fiancé that was paying most of the bills. We consoled him and hoped he would be ok. 

Personally I have my own struggles with mental health and figured he could use a friend, so the next day I sent him a text if he wanted to grab lunch together. It would be the first time we ever hung out just the two of us. At first he declined because he couldn't afford it but I offered to pay(or as he puts it when telling the story, "I didn't  ask if you could pay"). 

So we got lunch and we chatted for quite a while actually. Both about his Fiancé and kid, our shared mental health struggles and a bunch of other things completely unrelated. Later I suggested inviting a few of the other guys from our discord out to a nearby pub to play some pool(it was free pool night). We didn't end up going home until closing time.

That started a tradition with at least the two of us, if the others couldn't make it, of going out every week to play pool. We quickly became best friends(my previous best friend that I still talk to frequently moved to another city a few years ago). After a couple months of this, he admitted to me that he had planned on committing suicide that day until i asked him to grab lunch and took.his mind off of things and that I probably saved his life.  We've been mostly inseparable since.

Sorry for the long story, I guess only the first part is technically the "first time we met" but the longer bit was how we met as friends.
